help.intro: Intelligence routing picks a provider + model pair, or rejects the call with a reason. It does not read message text and does not call another model to decide.

contenders.title: Who enters the race
contenders.intro: A model only competes if it passes all of this:

list.provider: The provider is enabled, has credentials, and the responses adapter is active.
list.catalog: The model exists in the catalog and the catalog is fresh.
list.capabilities: It declares the capabilities the request asks for (tools, image, JSON, etc.). Unknown capability eliminates the candidate.
list.outputLimit: If the request asks for an output limit, that limit fits what the catalog declares.

contenders.footer: Provider health does not break ties or change the target. If more than one candidate remains without a rule that picks one, the response is ambiguous—not “the first in the list”.

winner.title: Who wins

explicitPair.title: Provider and model specified.
explicitPair.body: Only that pair. If the model exists only on another provider, reject. Do not switch providers.

providerOnly.title: Provider only.
providerOnly.body: Wins if exactly one eligible model remains on that provider. Zero or many: reject.

modelOnly.title: Model only.
modelOnly.body: Wins if exactly one eligible pair exists with that id. If the same id appears on multiple accounts of the same provider type, tie-break is weighted round-robin by quota (AW-RR). Different provider types stay ambiguous.

nothing.title: Nothing specified.
nothing.body: If OpenCode Go has exactly one eligible model, it wins. Otherwise, choose only if a single candidate remains hub-wide with fresh catalogs. Multiple candidates: reject.

winner.antigravityNoteLead: without an explicit provider only pins the provider when a single Antigravity account exists.

auto.title: aihub/auto
auto.bodyLead: That id is not a real model. The flow is: allowed list, then only models with contract proof for the request format (quota, cooldown, smoke, schema), then the pool with the highest quota weight, and within the pool the administrative order. The
auto.bodyEfficiencyTrail: profile pushes Gemini to the end on short calls. The
auto.bodyIntelligenceTrail: profile does not change order; it only records that there is no extra evidence.
